section_summary: This section contains wartime reports from Bern on declining Japanese cocoon and silk production, including a translated German newspaper survey of the silk industries in Japan and Japanese-occupied China. The survey describes falling output, changes in silk processing and pricing, Japanese control of Chinese mills, and shrinking export markets. A separate confidential State Department memorandum considers Department of Justice inquiries concerning a possible Logan Act prosecution arising from Raoul E. Desvernine's attempted Japanese-American barter negotiations.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 897 reporting Japanese cocoon-production estimates
subfiles.about: Reports German press figures for Japanese cocoon production and the declining number of individual silk producers.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 897: a Tokyo despatch in German press estimates autumn 1943 cocoons at 94,000 metric tons and 1943 total at 205,000, equal to 1942; producers fell by 104,000 to 1,120,000.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 7275: The silk industry in Japan and occupied China
subfiles.from: Hugh S. Fullerton, Counselor of Legation, for the U.S. Minister at Bern
subfiles.about: Transmits a translation of a German newspaper article on current conditions in the silk industries of Japan and occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 7275: the Bern Legation forwards a translation of a February 4, 1944 Kolnische Zeitung article on wartime silk industry conditions in Japan and occupied China.

subfiles.title: Japanese Silk Industry
subfiles.from: Kölnische Zeitung, translated and transmitted by the American Legation at Bern
subfiles.to: Department of State, as enclosure to despatch no. 7275
subfiles.about: Surveys falling silk production, altered processing and prices in Japan, and Japanese control and contraction of the silk industry in occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Japanese cocoon output fell after losing the U.S. market, policy stressed quantity, simplified grades and silk wool, and raw-silk prices rose with Manchuria and Indochina exports; in occupied China production declined as authorities favored cotton, Kachu controlled most mills, stocks piled up, and Guangdong output contracted.

subfiles.title: Duplicate despatch no. 7275: The silk industry in Japan and occupied China
subfiles.from: Hugh S. Fullerton, Counselor of Legation, for the U.S. Minister at Bern
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy transmitting a translation of a German newspaper article on silk production in Japan and occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Another copy of Despatch 7275 from Bern forwarding the February 4, 1944 Kolnische Zeitung article on Japanese and occupied-Chinese silk.

subfiles.title: Duplicate enclosure: Japanese Silk Industry
subfiles.from: Kölnische Zeitung, translated and transmitted by the American Legation at Bern
subfiles.to: Department of State, as enclosure to despatch no. 7275
subfiles.about: Duplicate translation describing wartime changes in the Japanese and occupied-Chinese silk industries.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate enclosure: declining Japanese cocoon output, volume over quality, expanded silk wool, changing prices and outlets, contraction in occupied China under Kachu's dominance, strict mill size limits, small stocks, weak demand and shipping shortages.

subfiles.title: Strictly confidential memorandum on the possible Logan Act prosecution of Raoul E. Desvernine
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs; drafting notation FE:Salisbury:MJK
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on Department of Justice inquiries connected with a possible prosecution of Desvernine for unauthorized Japanese-American barter negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Justice's Jesse Climenko, examining records of Raoul Desvernine's 1941 Japanese-American barter effort, raised a possible Logan Act prosecution and asked whether Acheson's memorandum and Hull's talk with Jouett Shouse could be used; Hackworth advised asking Shouse first and deferring the decision.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 7039 reporting further decline in Japanese cocoon production
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Legation at Bern
subfiles.about: Relays a German press report on the falling number of Japanese silk producers and reduced cocoon output.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 7039: a Tokyo despatch in German press reports 995,000 silk producers, down from 1,114,000, and cocoons of about 23.7 million kan against 29.4 million, blamed on food production, abandoned mulberry, war-industry labor transfers and cold weather.
